forum.title: How to tell if basement seepage is a pressurized pipe leak vs. rising groundwater table
forum.body: Before hiring a plumber to break slab concrete, test chlorine & temperature. Municipal supply leaks usually show trace free chlorine (0.5–2.0 ppm) on a DPD test strip and stay steady even when your water meter triangle stops? Wait—turn off all fixtures and check the low-flow leak dial on the city meter for 15 minutes. If the dial does NOT spin while water continues seeping at the cove joint after rain, you are dealing with hydrostatic groundwater.

replies.body: Adding to this: document the cove-joint weeping line with a ruler and timestamped photos over 48 hours. That exact evidence separates sudden pipe burst claims from excluded surface groundwater in insurance disputes.

forum.title: Insurance adjuster called standing drywall damage "long-term seepage" — how to respond with code citations
forum.body: Never accept a verbal denial on site. Ask the adjuster in writing for the specific moisture-gradient readings and fungal growth staging report supporting "long-term." Under IICRC S500 standards, secondary microbial growth can begin within 24–48 hours of a sudden supply failure. Use the AI Insurance Verbiage tab in insights to draft a factual rebuttal.

forum.title: Termite tenting vs. localized borates/hotspot treatment — real cost and chemical persistence breakdown
forum.body: Sharing our experience: structural fumigation (sulfuryl fluoride tenting) clears hidden drywood colonies in inaccessible rafters in 72 hours with zero residual odor, whereas hotspot orange oil / fipronil only treats visible galleries. Always demand a Wood Destroying Organism (WDO) diagram before choosing.
